title: Cell theory, microscopes and magnification; Cell specialisation, tissues, organs
specRef: CC2(c), CC2-SP1, CC2-SP2, C2.4-SP3 and others; CC2(d)
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: CE01a#t4 term and clue written for the game; CE07a#t1 term and clue written for the game; CE01a#t2 term and clue written for the game; CE01a#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: CE01a#N.6, CE07a#N.3a, CE01a#N.9, CE07a#N.10b, CE01a#N.12, CE07a#N.11.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Stage micrometer
items.clue: A slide with a real scale, often 1 mm in 100 divisions

items.label: Zygote
items.clue: The single cell from which a whole body is built up by mitosis

items.label: Scale bar
items.clue: A line on an image labelled with the actual length it represents

items.label: Magnification
items.clue: Image size divided by actual size; written with no unit, e.g. ×2000

questions.stem: In a photomicrograph taken at a magnification of ×2000, a red blood cell measures 15 mm across. What is the actual width of the cell?

options.text: 7.5 µm

questions.explanation: Actual size = 15 mm ÷ 2000 = 0.0075 mm, which is 7.5 µm (1 mm = 1000 µm): the typical diameter of a red blood cell.

questions.stem: In a human, a neuron and a liver cell are both descended by mitosis from the same zygote. What is the difference between them once they have differentiated?

options.text: They express different subsets of the same complete set of genes.
They have kept different sets of genes and discarded the rest.
They were set on different paths inside from fertilisation.
They differ only until the body needs to swap them over.

questions.explanation: All cells produced by mitosis from the zygote inherit the full genome. The neuron switches on the genes for its proteins and the liver cell a different set, while both keep every gene.

questions.stem: With the ×40 objective lens in place, 40 divisions of an eyepiece graticule line up exactly with 100 µm on a stage micrometer. Using the same objective, a cell spans 44 graticule divisions. What is the actual length of the cell in millimetres?

options.text: 1.1 mm

questions.explanation: 100 µm ÷ 40 = 2.5 µm per division with this objective. 44 × 2.5 µm = 110 µm = 0.11 mm.

questions.stem: The wall of the stomach contains epithelium, smooth muscle and connective tissue. Together they digest and churn food. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Epithelium, muscle and connective tissue are each organs, as each has a function.
The stomach is an organ system, as it contains several different tissues.
The stomach is an organ: several tissues working together for an overall function.
Epithelium is not a tissue if it contains goblet cells as well as other cells.

questions.explanation: Epithelium, muscle and connective tissue each do one job; together they perform digestion, the stomach's overall function.

questions.stem: A micrograph shows a pollen grain 60 mm across. A scale bar on the micrograph is 20 mm long and is labelled 10 µm. What is the actual diameter of the pollen grain?

options.text: 3 µm
30 µm
60 µm
120 µm

questions.explanation: Magnification = 20 000 µm ÷ 10 µm = ×2000. Actual size = 60 000 µm ÷ 2000 = 30 µm.

questions.stem: In a hypothetical species of plant, leaf cells make large amounts of a protein that binds chlorophyll, but the root cells of the same plant make none of it. Which statement best explains this difference?

options.text: In root cells, the base sequence of the gene has been changed, and the gene no longer codes for the protein.
Both cell types carry the gene for the protein, but it is expressed in leaf cells and not in root cells.
Root cells have lost the gene for the protein from their DNA because they did not use it.
Root cells do not need the protein, so they choose not to make it, unlike the cells of leaves.
